question: Moatsu festival of Nagaland is celebrated by which of the following tribes?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Ao tribe__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Moatsu Festival:-**

 
 
• **It is a post-harvest festival celebrated by the Ao Naga people of Nagaland, India.**
 
• It is held annually in May for three days, marking the end of the agricultural season and the beginning of a new one.
 
• The festival is a time for the community to come together, celebrate their rich culture and heritage, and give thanks for a bountiful harvest. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhil tribe:-**

 
 
• It is one of the largest indigenous groups in India, inhabiting mostly the western and central regions of the country, particularly in the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.
 
• They are believed to be the descendants of the ancient inhabitants of the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Munda tribe:-**
 
 
• It is another prominent indigenous group in India, primarily concentrated in the eastern states of Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• They are believed to be one of the earliest inhabitants of the Chota Nagpur Plateau region.
 
 
 
• **Bodo tribe:-**
 
 
• It is a significant indigenous group in Northeast India, predominantly inhabiting the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, and Meghalaya.
 
• They are believed to be part of the Tibeto-Burman linguistic group.
